leads.posting: Mesa School of Business raises Rs 110 Cr in equity and debt. Startup-focused business school and edtech company Mesa School of Business has raised Rs 110 crore, comprising around Rs 85 crore in Series A equity funding co-led by Dharana Capital and existing investor Elevation Capital, and Rs 25 crore in venture debt from InnoVen Capital and Alteria Capital. The company is also backed by founders including Kunal Shah of CRED, Vidit Aatrey of Meesho, Abhiraj Bhal of Urban Company, and Vijay Shekhar Sharma of Paytm. According to the company, the fresh funding round values it at Rs 385 crore. Entrackr had exclusively reported on Mesa School of Business’s Series A funding last month. The proceeds will be used to invest in an AI-first curriculum for existing programmes, launch and scale new programmes, and build strategic partnerships with the startup ecosystem, the company said in a press release. Co-founded in 2023 by Ankit Agarwal and Varun Limaye, Mesa School of Business offers residential programmes for undergraduates, fresh graduates and early-career professionals. The Bengaluru-based institution aims to prepare students for leadership and entrepreneurship in an AI-first world. The company said every student builds and runs a small business and learns to use AI to develop and launch a technology product. Mesa has grown from a single postgraduate cohort to over 550 students across three programmes: a one-year Post Graduate Programme in Startup Leadership, a four-year undergraduate programme in business and entrepreneurship, and Forge, a one-year programme for fresh graduates. Mesa said over 100 founders have taught on campus, while students have worked on more than 200 projects with startups. Its alumni pursue full-time roles at startups or start their own businesses. According to the company, students from its first two postgraduate cohorts secured an average CTC of Rs 26 lakh, while the top 25% averaged Rs 36.5 lakh. leads.posting: Mesa School Bags ₹110 Cr To Launch New On-Campus Courses. Bengaluru-based Mesa School of Business has raised ₹110 Cr ($11.4 Mn) in its Series A funding round in a mix of debt and equity. The round pegged the business school at a post-money valuation of ₹385 Cr ($40 Mn), cofounder Ankit Agarwal told Inc42. While the ₹85 Cr equity round was co-led by Dharana Capital and existing backer Elevation Capital, the remaining ₹25 Cr was raised via venture debt from InnoVen Capital and Alteria Capital. Mesa plans to utilise the fresh capital to strengthen its leadership team, integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into its programmes, deepen partnerships with startups and launch new courses. Founded in 2023 by Agarwal and Varun Limaye, Mesa offers on-campus educational programmes for individuals. It currently offers three full-time programmes targeting early-career professionals, fresh graduates and undergraduate students. While the startup charges ₹25.4 Lakh in tuition fees for its one-year post-graduate programme, its one-year Forge programme for fresh graduates has a starting fees of ₹15.4 Lakh. The undergraduate programme costs ₹48 Lakh over four years. Training Talent For Startups Despite being one of India’s fastest-growing employment segments, the local startup ecosystem continues to face a talent gap. Speaking with Inc42, Agarwal said that the talent paucity is especially acute in non-technical roles, which account for nearly 80% of jobs in the sector. While graduates from premier institutions often have established recruitment pathways into startups, students without access to such networks, Agarwal said, lack a structured route to enter the startup ecosystem. “If you want to go and work in a startup, there is no one place which sort of builds the right network,” he said. leads.posting: D2C Brand Boldfit Raises ₹400 Cr From Bharat Value Fund For Retail Expansion. D2C fitness and sportswear brand Boldfit has raised around ₹400 Cr (about $41.8 Mn) from Bharat Value Fund as part of its Series B funding round. The fund is a Category II AIF managed by The Wealth Company Alternates, part of Pantomath Group. Boldfit said the investment would support nationwide retail expansion, product innovation, and manufacturing. It also plans to pursue selective acquisitions to strengthen its presence and capabilities across categories. Founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani, Bengaluru-based Boldfit sells performance sportswear, athletic footwear, sports equipment, and fitness essentials. The startup claims to serve more than 2 Cr customers annually across India. “We’re building a deeply integrated sports business, investing in product innovation, manufacturing excellence and nationwide retail to create the scale and capabilities required to serve India’s sporting ambitions,” Bihani said. The retail push builds on plans outlined during its ₹110 Cr funding round from Bessemer Venture Partners in November 2024, when Boldfit said it intended to open offline stores over the following 12-18 months. Following the latest round, Boldfit’s total funding to date has risen to over ₹510 Cr. The startup also counts cricketer KL Rahul and former tennis player Sania Mirza among its investors. India’s fitness and sports goods market is estimated to be worth $16 Bn and is projected to reach $35 Bn by FY31, driven by rising disposable incomes, growing health awareness, and wider access through ecommerce, organised retail, and quick commerce channels. As a result, Indian sportswear and athleisure startups are seeing a lot of investor interest. In June, sportswear startup Agilitas raised ₹225 Cr funding round from Nexus Venture Partners and Rainmatter, with Nexus investing ₹200 Cr and Rainmatter contributing ₹25 Cr.
